sections.title: About Us
sections.intro: From a small town on the coast of Gujarat to tables across the world, Ankur has grown into a trusted salt manufacturer in India over more than 30 years. We do not just make salt. We make salt the right way.

src.alt: Ankur Chemfood leadership receiving the Bhartiya Udyog Ratan Award

paragraphs.value: In 1994, in Gandhidham, Kutch, the Champalal Group saw an opportunity hiding in plain sight.

India had one of the richest natural salt belts in the world. But the salt reaching Indian homes was far from what families deserved in terms of purity, nutrition, and quality. Ankur Chemfood Limited was started to fix exactly that.

We set up on the coast of Gujarat, steps away from India's most productive marine salt region and within reach of two of the country's biggest ports. From day one, we chose to do things properly. Swiss technology. Automated machinery. Triple refinement. No shortcuts.

items.caption: Founded, Champalal Group
items.description: Ankur Chemfood Limited begins operations in Gandhidham, Gujarat. Manufacturing starts using fully automated Swiss technology, making us one of the most advanced salt producers in India from the very beginning.

items.caption: First ISO certified salt maker
items.description: Ankur Salt becomes the first ISO certified refined salt manufacturer in India. A milestone that set the standard for the entire industry.

image_src.alt: Late 1990s: First ISO certified salt maker

items.caption: Five plants, NH 8A
items.description: We expand to five manufacturing plants on National Highway 8A, near Deendayal Port Trust (Kandla) and Adani Port (Mundra). Our capacity grows. Our export reach grows with it.

items.caption: Dr. Salt & DFS IQ+ launched
items.description: Years of research and development lead to two new products. We launch Dr. Salt, a low sodium salt made for people who need to watch their sodium intake. We also introduce DFS IQ+ Salt, a double fortified salt that carries both iron and iodine. These were not trends. They were genuine responses to real health needs in Indian homes.

image_src.alt: 2004 to 2006: Dr. Salt and DFS IQ+ launched

items.caption: ICCIDD endorsement
items.description: Ankur Salt becomes the first salt brand in India to receive endorsement from ICCIDD, the International Council for Control of Iodine Deficiency Disorders. A global health recognition that no other Indian salt brand had earned before us.

items.caption: Emerging India Award nomination
items.description: Ankur Chemfood Limited is nominated among the top three companies in India for the Emerging India Award by ICICI Bank, CRISIL and CNBC. The award ceremony is held in Macau, Hong Kong.

items.caption: 1,000+ clients worldwide
items.description: More than 30 years since we started, Ankur Salt has over 1,000 corporate clients, dealers and distributors around the world. Our five plants run at a combined capacity of 10 lakh tons per year. We hold the Bharatiya Udyog Ratna Award and continue to be certified under ISO 9001:2015 and FSSC 22000, the gold standard in food safety.

sections.title: Quality & Certificates
sections.intro: Every batch of Ankur Salt is tested and verified before it leaves our plants. Here's exactly how we refine it, and what each of our certifications actually means.

sections.heading: Manufacturing Process
sections.subheading: From raw salt to your table: six steps, the same way every time.

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.description: Raw salt is sourced from our own fields on India's marine salt belt in Gandhidham, Gujarat, near Kandla and Mundra ports.

steps.title: Washing & Crushing
steps.description: Raw crystals are picked clean of foreign particles, washed with magnetic separation to remove metal fragments, and centrifuged to separate pure brine before crushing brings every crystal to a uniform size.

steps.title: Refining
steps.description: Fully automated machinery based on Swiss technology refines the salt, drying it in a fluidised bed drier at a controlled 170°C to 260°C to reach purity greater than 98% NaCl.

steps.title: Iodisation
steps.description: Iodine is added and mixed to a controlled 20 ppm to 30 ppm content, monitored continuously so every batch stays within range.

steps.title: Quality Testing
steps.description: Before packaging, salt passes through a final screening stage where an 8mm screen and magnetic separator catch any oversized or metallic particles, then our in house QC lab runs more than 12 additional tests on every batch.

steps.title: Packaging & Dispatch
steps.description: Once cleared, the salt is sealed, stacked and loaded for dispatch to distributors, retailers and export markets around the world.

sections.heading: Certifications Explained
sections.subheading: What each certification actually means, not just a logo on a page.

sections.name: ISO 22000-2018
sections.description: Means our processes, from sourcing to packaging, are consistently managed and audited to meet an international quality standard, not checked just once.

sections.name: FSSC 22000
sections.description: One of the most widely recognised food safety certifications globally. It confirms our food safety practices meet standards accepted by retailers and food businesses worldwide.

sections.name: BIS IS:7224
sections.description: The Indian government's official specification for edible common salt. Meeting it means our salt meets India's defined standards for purity and safety.

sections.name: FSSAI
sections.issuer: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
sections.description: India's food safety regulator. Our FSSAI license means we are registered, inspected and authorised to manufacture and sell food grade salt in India.

sections.name: Halal Certified
sections.description: Confirms our manufacturing process meets Islamic dietary requirements, verified by an accredited certifying body, important for many of our export markets.

data.title: How to Choose Iodised Salt for Everyday Cooking
data.excerpt: Choosing an iodised salt takes more than checking the label for the word "iodised." Here's what fortification, purity, grain quality, and manufacturing standards actually tell you about a product.
data.meta_description: Looking for the best cooking salt? Learn how to choose refined, free-flowing iodised salt based on iodine fortification, vacuum-evaporated purity, and storage.

image.alt: Ankur Salt product packaging displaying refined free flow iodised salt next to a wooden bowl of white cooking salt and fresh vegetables.

children.text: Salt is a basic ingredient used in kitchens and food production around the world. It is used to season food and, in the case of iodised salt, to provide iodine through a commonly consumed ingredient.

However, choosing an iodised salt involves more than looking for the word "iodised" on a package. Factors such as iodine fortification, purity, processing, grain characteristics, quality control, packaging, and storage can influence the suitability of a product.

For consumers, food manufacturers, distributors, and international buyers, understanding these factors can make it easier to evaluate an iodised salt based on its actual characteristics and the capabilities of its manufacturer.
What Is Iodised Salt?
Iodised salt is salt that has been fortified with iodine. Iodine is an essential nutrient required by the body for normal thyroid function and healthy development.
Salt is commonly used as a carrier for iodine because it is consumed regularly and provides a practical way of increasing iodine intake across populations. The
World Health Organization (WHO)
recognises salt iodisation as an effective strategy for preventing iodine deficiency disorders.

Iodisation is not intended to encourage greater salt consumption. Salt intake should still be kept within appropriate dietary limits. Instead, it allows iodine to be provided through an ingredient that is already widely used in food preparation.
It is also important to distinguish iodisation from refining. Iodised describes the addition of iodine, while refined describes the processing that the salt undergoes.
What Should You Look for When Choosing Iodised Salt?
The right choice depends on the intended application, but several characteristics are useful when evaluating an iodised salt.
Iodine Fortification

Check whether the product is properly iodised and whether the manufacturer provides clear information about its iodine content or fortification specifications. For commercial buyers, documented specifications can be especially important when consistency between batches is required.
Purity and Quality

Specifications such as sodium chloride content, moisture, and water-insoluble matter provide useful information about the product. Food businesses may also need to consider applicable food safety requirements, certifications, and quality-control practices based on their market and intended use.
Grain and Flow Characteristics

Grain size and flow characteristics can influence how salt behaves during handling and use. Consistent grains can make dispensing easier, while suitable flow characteristics can support handling, weighing, blending, and processing in commercial applications.
Packaging and Storage

Packaging should protect the product from moisture and contamination while being appropriate for its intended market and application. Storage is equally important because excessive moisture can cause grains to stick together and affect handling.
Does Refined Salt Mean the Same as Iodised Salt?
No. Refined and iodised describe different characteristics of a salt product.
Refined salt refers to salt that has undergone processing to remove impurities and achieve defined quality and physical characteristics.
Iodised salt refers to salt that has been fortified with iodine.
A product can therefore be both refined and iodised. Ankur Salt is positioned as a
refined, free-flow iodised salt
, with vacuum evaporation used as part of its refining process.
This distinction is useful when comparing products because processing and fortification address different aspects of the finished product.
Why Does Free-Flow Salt Matter?
Salt can interact with moisture from its surrounding environment. Under humid conditions, the grains can begin sticking together and become more difficult to handle.

Free-flow characteristics can therefore be useful in both domestic and commercial settings. For consumers, they can make dispensing and measuring easier. For food manufacturers and other commercial users, suitable flow characteristics can support smoother handling and processing.

Ankur describes its Free Flow Iodised Salt as a product designed to maintain loose grains, including under humid conditions. The importance of this characteristic depends on the application and storage environment, so buyers should consider how and where the product will be transported, stored, and used.
What Makes Ankur's Manufacturing Approach Relevant to Buyers?
A product specification tells only part of the story. The manufacturing and quality systems behind the product can also provide useful information when evaluating a salt supplier.
Ankur Chemfood Limited

has been manufacturing salt since 1994, with its operations based in Gandhidham on Gujarat's marine salt belt. The company states that its manufacturing began with fully automated machinery based on Swiss technology.

Ankur currently operates five manufacturing plants and states that its combined production capacity is 10 lakh tons per year. Its location near Kandla and Mundra ports also supports its export operations and international supply network.

The company describes a manufacturing process that includes sourcing raw salt, washing and crushing, refining, iodisation, quality testing and packaging. It also states that its salt passes through final screening and magnetic separation before undergoing more than 12 additional tests in its in-house quality-control laboratory.
Ankur's
quality and certifications
include ISO 22000:2018, FSSC 22000, BIS IS:7224, FSSAI and Halal certification. The company also highlights an ICCIDD endorsement received in 2008 for its iodisation practices.
For
international buyers

, these manufacturing capabilities, quality systems and certifications can provide useful evidence when assessing a supplier. However, certifications do not replace the need to review product specifications and confirm compliance with the regulations of the destination market.
Ankur Salt for Everyday Food Use
Ankur Salt is positioned as a
refined, free-flow iodised salt
for everyday food use. The individual product page provides specific information about its composition, physical characteristics, processing, and pack formats.

According to the current Ankur Salt product page, the product has a minimum sodium chloride content of 99%, maximum moisture of 0.5%, maximum water-insoluble matter of 0.5%, and a minimum iodine content of 20 ppm at production, or as per party requirement. The page also specifies that at least 98% of the salt should pass through an 850-micron sieve.
The product is manufactured using a vacuum evaporation process and is stated to be FSSAI compliant.

These product-level specifications should be considered separately from Ankur's broader manufacturing capabilities and company-wide certifications. For buyers, this distinction is important because supplier credentials and individual product specifications answer different questions.

International buyers, importers, and distributors should evaluate the product against the requirements of their destination country, intended application, packaging requirements, and applicable food regulations.
How to Store Iodised Salt Properly
Proper storage helps maintain the intended physical condition of salt after manufacturing and packaging.

For smaller quantities, keep the product sealed and store it in a clean, dry location away from excessive moisture and direct heat. Once opened, a suitable well-sealed container can help protect the product from humid conditions.

For commercial and bulk handling, storage conditions become even more important. The product should be protected from moisture, contamination, and unsuitable environmental conditions during transportation and warehousing.
Good storage practices should therefore be considered throughout the supply chain, from production and distribution to final use.
Conclusion

Choosing an iodised salt involves more than checking whether iodine has been added. The intended application, iodine fortification, purity, processing, grain characteristics, manufacturing controls, certifications, packaging, and storage conditions can all contribute to an informed purchasing decision.

Ankur Salt combines defined product specifications with a manufacturing operation built around automated Swiss technology, refining, in-house quality testing, and established food-safety systems. Its manufacturing and export infrastructure also supports supply beyond the domestic market.

For consumers, food businesses, distributors, and international buyers, the most useful approach is to evaluate the actual product specifications alongside the systems and evidence behind the manufacturer. This provides a more complete basis for choosing an iodised salt than relying on a product label alone.

data.title: Why Iodised Salt Still Matters: What the ICCIDD Endorsement Actually Means
data.excerpt: Iodine deficiency looks like a solved problem in India, but the numbers behind it tell a different story. Universal salt iodisation is still the frontline defence, and it only works if every batch is consistent.
data.meta_description: Iodine deficiency isn't solved in India yet. Why universal salt iodisation is still the frontline defence, and what the ICCIDD endorsement means.

image.alt: Fresh food prepared with iodised salt

children.text: Iodine deficiency disorders can look like a solved problem, but that only holds up until you remember the solution works only if every household is actually getting iodine, batch after batch, without fail. That's the entire point of universal salt iodisation, and it's why we treat it as a manufacturing discipline, not a marketing line.
The public health case for iodisation

Iodine is essential for thyroid function, and thyroid hormones govern everything from metabolism to early childhood cognitive development. Because iodine occurs naturally in only a few foods, salt, something nearly every household already buys, became the most effective way to close the gap at a population scale.
What the ICCIDD endorsement actually means

The International Council for Control of Iodine Deficiency Disorders (ICCIDD) is a global health body focused on eliminating iodine deficiency. Their endorsement isn't a logo you can simply apply for; it means independent health experts have reviewed our iodisation process itself, from dosing to consistency. Ankur Salt is the only Indian salt brand to hold this endorsement.
How we keep it consistent, batch after batch

Consistency is the hard part of iodisation, not the chemistry. Every batch passes through our in house QC lab, where iodine content is checked against a controlled 35 ppm target before packaging. It isn't sampled occasionally; it's monitored continuously.
Iodine is added and mixed to a controlled 35 ppm content on every batch
In house QC lab staff run more than 12 tests before anything is packaged
Refining happens on fully automated, Swiss technology machinery to keep dosing consistent
The bottom line
A bag of iodised salt is only as good as the process behind it. The certifications and the endorsement exist because that process is checked by people who don't work for us.

data.title: Inside Our Triple Refining Process: From Raw Crystal to 99.28% Purity
data.excerpt: Six steps stand between raw salt on our own fields in Gujarat and the bag on your shelf. Here's exactly what happens at each one, and why we run it the same way every time.
data.meta_description: The six steps between raw salt on our Gujarat fields and the pack on your shelf, and how triple refining reaches 99.28% purity every batch.

image.alt: Salt flats on Gujarat's marine salt belt

children.text: "Triple refined" is a phrase that shows up on a lot of packaging. On ours, it describes six specific steps that happen the same way on every batch. It isn't marketing shorthand for "processed."
Step one: sourcing from our own fields

Raw salt is sourced from our own fields on India's marine salt belt in Gandhidham, Gujarat, near Kandla and Mundra ports. Owning the source is what lets us control quality from the very first stage, rather than inheriting whatever variability a third party supplier hands us.
Washing, crushing, and refining

Raw crystals are washed to remove impurities and crushed to a uniform size before refining begins. From there, fully automated machinery based on Swiss technology refines the salt into Triple Refined Free Flow Iodised Salt, reaching 99.28% NaCl purity.
Iodisation, tested not assumed

Iodine is added and mixed to a controlled 35 ppm content, monitored continuously so every batch stays within range. Before packaging, every batch passes through our in house QC lab, where qualified staff run more than 12 tests.
Packaging and dispatch

Once cleared, the salt is sealed and dispatched to distributors, retailers and export markets around the world. It's the same six step process whether it's headed to a shop three hours from our plants or a container ship at Mundra.
Why the process matters more than the marketing

Anyone can print "triple refined" on a bag. What actually backs that claim is a repeatable process, audited machinery, and a QC lab that tests every batch before it leaves. That's exactly what our ISO 9001:2015 and FSSC 22000 certifications verify.

data.title: What FSSC 22000 and ISO 9001:2015 Actually Mean for Your Kitchen
data.excerpt: Certifications can read like a logo wall. Here's what each one on our packaging actually guarantees, and why we hold all of them instead of just the minimum required to sell in India.
data.meta_description: What each certification on our salt packaging actually guarantees, and why we hold FSSC 22000, ISO 9001:2015 and more beyond the legal minimum.

children.text: Certifications can start to look like a logo wall, collected and displayed without much thought to what any of them actually verify. Here's what each one on our packaging really guarantees.
ISO 9001:2015: process discipline, not a check done just once

ISO 9001:2015 means our processes, from sourcing to packaging, are consistently managed and audited to meet an international quality standard. It's not a single inspection passed once; it's an ongoing audit trail.
FSSC 22000: the standard retailers actually check for

FSSC 22000 (Food Safety System Certification) is one of the most widely recognised food safety certifications globally. It confirms our food safety practices meet standards accepted by retailers and food businesses worldwide, which is often the first document an international buyer asks for.
BIS IS:7224 and FSSAI: the Indian baseline

BIS IS:7224 is the Bureau of Indian Standards' official specification for edible common salt. Meeting it means our salt meets India's defined standards for purity and safety. FSSAI registration means we're inspected and authorised by India's food safety regulator to manufacture and sell food grade salt.
ISO 9001:2015: quality management system, audited continuously
FSSC 22000: globally recognised food safety certification
BIS IS:7224: India's official edible salt specification
FSSAI: India's food safety regulator registration
ICCIDD Endorsement: independent review of our iodisation process
Halal Certified: verified by an accredited certifying body
Why we chose to stack all of them

No single certification covers everything an international buyer, a domestic retailer, and a health regulator each care about. Holding all six means we don't ask a buyer to take our word for it. There's a document behind every claim.

data.title: The Truth About Iodised Salt
data.excerpt: Why iodisation still matters for everyday health, and how to tell real protection from marketing.

image.alt: Ankur Salt Free Flow Iodised pack

children.text: Every packet of iodised salt makes the same quiet promise: that the iodine on the label is actually in the salt, in a dose that matters, batch after batch. That promise is easy to write on a pack and much harder to keep, which is really the whole story of what iodisation is.
Why iodine is added to salt in the first place

Iodine is essential for thyroid function, and the thyroid governs metabolism and, in children, cognitive development. Because iodine occurs naturally in only a handful of foods, salt became the standard carrier for it worldwide, simply because nearly every household already buys salt regularly.
What's actually in the bag

Free Flow Iodised is refined to at least 99% NaCl and carries a minimum of 30 ppm iodine at production. That figure isn't a one-time lab result; it's the target every batch is checked against before it's packed.
How to tell real protection from marketing

Iodine content and certification marks are printed on every pack for a reason: check them, rather than taking a brand's word for it. Ankur Salt was the first ISO certified refined salt manufacturer in India, and in 2008 became the first Indian salt brand endorsed by the ICCIDD (International Council for Control of Iodine Deficiency Disorders).
Look for the iodine content figure on the pack, not just the word "iodised"
Store salt away from direct heat and moisture, both of which degrade iodine over time
Buy only what you'll use within a reasonable time rather than stockpiling for years
The bottom line
Iodisation only works if it's consistent, batch after batch, which is why we treat it as a manufacturing discipline rather than a claim on a label. Real salt. Nothing hidden.

data.title: 5 Ways to Cook With Rock Salt
data.excerpt: Sendha namak isn't just for fasting. Here's how it earns a permanent spot in the kitchen.

image.alt: Ankur Rock Salt pack with natural rock salt chunks

children.text: Ankur Rock Salt, or sendha namak, shows up in most Indian kitchens once a year for Navratri and then goes back in the cupboard. That's a shame, because its natural, unrefined character makes it useful well beyond fasting season.
What makes rock salt different

Unlike our refined, iodised ranges, Ankur Rock Salt is natural and unrefined, around 85 to 90% sodium chloride with naturally occurring trace minerals like iron, potassium and magnesium. No iodine is added. That's exactly why it's the traditional choice for fasting and religious offerings, and why it tastes noticeably milder than table salt.
1. Vrat and fasting recipes

This is its best-known role, the traditional choice for Navratri, Ekadashi and other fasting occasions, used in place of iodised salt in vrat-friendly dishes like sabudana khichdi and kuttu ka atta puris.
2. As a finishing salt
Its milder, more mineral flavour works well sprinkled over grilled vegetables or roasted potatoes just before serving, where you taste the salt itself rather than cooking it into the dish.
3. In pickling and preserving
Rock salt's coarser, natural crystal is a common choice for home pickling, where a milder, unrefined salt is preferred to a heavily processed one.
4. For religious offerings and prasad
Used in rituals and traditional ceremonies for generations, it remains the default choice for prasad and religious offerings across much of India.
5. In Ayurvedic cooking
Valued in Ayurvedic practice specifically for its natural, unrefined form, it's often the salt of choice in Ayurvedic kitchens for everyday, milder recipes.
The bottom line
Rock salt doesn't need to be a once-a-year ingredient. Keep a pack in rotation alongside your everyday iodised salt, and reach for it whenever a recipe calls for something milder and more mineral.

children.text: Namak kam hi khaaye, par achha khaaye: eat less salt, but eat salt that's real. That's less a slogan than the actual habit worth building, and it has less to do with cutting salt out than with using it with a bit more attention.
What mindful salt use actually looks like
Most people season on autopilot, a shake while cooking, another at the table, without tasting in between. Mindful use just means slowing that down enough to notice how much you're actually adding.
Small habits, real difference
Season in stages while cooking and taste before adding more, instead of salting once at the start
Measure with a spoon occasionally, just to recalibrate what a "pinch" actually means in your kitchen
Choose the grade for the job: Free Flow Iodised for everyday cooking, Dr. Salt if you're actively moderating sodium
Season at the table sparingly; food that's well seasoned in the pot rarely needs much more

Using less only helps if what you're using is worth using. Triple refined, tested in-house batch by batch, and iodised to a checked standard, not just labelled as such.
The bottom line

Eating mindfully isn't about giving salt up. It's about paying enough attention that every pinch is doing something for the dish, and choosing salt you don't have to think twice about. Real salt. Nothing hidden.
